narrative.overview:
The docs behave like one developer tool that a reader already has open. Slim chrome, keyboard shortcuts shown as keycaps, a status bar for a footer, and search that opens as a command palette all come from native desktop tooling. Real code is the main visual material, and the home page previews it inside a package palette.

The system is dark only and dense. Three graphite steps and 1px borders carry all structure. Colour appears in small amounts, and each colour has a job. Tiny square markers show position and state, so no icon set or illustration is needed beyond the puffin logo in the header.

The world rejects the SaaS landing page, meaning a hero with a mascot and a grid of feature cards. The site runs on MkDocs Material, and every token maps onto Material's variables, so generated API pages inherit the same look.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only, with no theme toggle.
Geist for text and chrome, Geist Mono for anything a developer would type or read as a machine value.
1px borders and tonal steps instead of shadows at rest.
Square markers, compact rectangular badges and keycaps.
A 140ms state transition on almost every interactive element.

rules.name: The Label Ground Rule
rules.body: Label Grey sits on Graphite Ground only. Small text on a panel or a raised step uses Secondary Grey, because Label Grey drops below 4.5:1 there.

rules.name: The Decoration Rule
rules.body: Decoration Grey never carries information a reader needs to read. If removing it would lose meaning, the element needs Secondary Grey.

rules.name: The Purple Rule
rules.body: Purple means a command, the CLI, or a Python keyword. Links and buttons stay teal or neutral.

rules.name: The Mono Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is for code, commands, shortcuts, statuses and identifiers. Everything else, including every label a person wrote, is Geist.

rules.name: The Root Rule
rules.body: The html element is pinned at 125%, which is 20px at the browser default, and Material's wide-screen growth is off. So .05rem is 1px, and every rem value in this file assumes that root.

rules.name: The Float Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the element sits above the page. Panels in the document flow, including the header, stay flat.

rules.name: The Square Rule
rules.body: State is marked with a tiny square, not a dot, stripe or icon. Teal is current, Decoration Grey is idle, amber is a warning or alpha status.

dos: Do keep the page dark, using only the three graphite steps for grounds.
Do use 1px Hairline borders (#34373b) and thin rules to separate things.
Do set commands, shortcuts, statuses, package names and file names in Geist Mono.
Do mark the current item with a 5px or 6px teal square.
Do show a keycap only when the shortcut works.
Do write rem values against the 20px root, where .05rem is 1px.
Do use Secondary Grey (#92979e) for small text on Panel Graphite or Raised Graphite.
Do map new colours through the `--cw-*` tokens and Material's `--md-*` variables, so generated API pages inherit them.
donts: Don't add a light theme or a theme toggle.
Don't build a hero with a mascot or a grid of feature cards. The puffin stays in the header as the logo.
Don't use Decoration Grey (#686d74) for text a reader needs.
Don't put Label Grey (#7f858c) on Panel Graphite or Raised Graphite.
Don't use purple for links, buttons or general emphasis.
Don't raise amber's saturation, or use it for anything other than warnings, alpha status and syntax values.
Don't divide page sections with background bands.
Don't put a shadow on a panel in the document flow, other than the palette's contact shadow.
Don't set uppercase or tracked labels in HTML chrome.
Don't use radii above 10px, or pill shapes.
